1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To provide guidelines for safe medication management and administration to patients.

2.0 SCOPE:-

2.1 Hospital wide

3.0 RESPONSIBILTY:

3.1 Doctors ,

3.2 Nursing staff

4.0 ABBREVIATION:

4.1 NABH : National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare providers

4.2 MOM : Management of Medication

5.0 DEFINITION: Medication management is medical care provided by Hospital whose aim is to optimize drug therapy and improve therapeutic outcomes for patients

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1Medications are administered by those who are permitted to do so.

7.2Prepared medication is labeled prior to preparation of a second drug.

7.3Patient is identified prior to administration

7.4Medication is verified from the order prior to administration.

7.5 Dosage is verified from the order prior to administration.

7.6 Route is verified from the order prior to administration.

7.7 Timing is verified from the order prior to administration.

7.8 Medication administration is documented.

7.9 Policies and procedures govern patients’ self-administration of medication.

7.10 Documented policies and procedures govern patients medications brought from outside the organization.

8.0 PROCEDURE:-

8.1 The individual who administers the medication is responsible for ensuring that the right medicine with right dose is administered to the right patient through the right route at the right time. All medications are administered as ordered by the doctors, by an authorized health care professional. A registered nurse Panchkarma therapist is approved to administer medications to the patient as ordered by the physician. If the medical staff member authorized to administer the medication has questions concerning the doctor’s order, he/she should consult the doctor or pharmacist prior to administering the medication.

8..2 Prepared medication is labeled prior to preparation of a second drug. E.g. while preparing basti dravya, the first yoga is prepared & labelled and then the subsequent yogas should be prepared & labelled

8..3 Identification shall be done by unique identification number or OPD number or IPD number or by name.

8.4 Staff administering medications goes through the treatment orders before administration of the medication and then only administers them. Staff checks the general appearance of the medication (e.g. broken tablet, clumped choorna etc.) before dispensing. If any of the parameters with respect to an order namely name, dose, route or frequency/time are missing/incomplete the medication administration shall be deferred. However, to ensure that patient care does not suffer a verbal order may be got from the treating doctor followed by ratification of the same (refer to MOM4e).In case of high alert medication(s), the verification shall be done by at least two staff (Paricharika-Nurse, Paricharaka-doctor or Paricharakadoctor) independently

8.5 Dosage is verified from the order prior to administration.

8.6 Route is verified from the order prior to administration

8.7 Timing is verified from the order prior to administration. Hospital has explained short form as gm for gram, mg for milligram, ml for milliliter, OD for once a day BD for twice a day, TDS for thrice a day, QID for four times a day, HS for at bedtime, SOS for as and when required

8.8 Medication administration is done in a standard format and it includes the name of the medication, dosage, route of administration, timing and the name and signature of the person who has administered the medication.

8.9 Self-administration of injectable drugs are not be permitted in the Inpatient care areas. Patients own oral medications brought in by the patients who are on chronic therapy (e.g. Conditions like Hypertension, Diabetes mellitus, Cancer, TB) are known to the treating physician and will be allowed to administer to the patient under the supervision and certification of treating physician, such medications are also be recorded in patient’s record.

8.10 Drugs bought from outside the organization are not allowed. In case of non-availability of some drugs, this may be allowed. Bill, Label, Dose and Expiry date are verified before administering to patient. Doctor or nurse are educate the patients and the family members about safe and effective use of medication and about the food-drug interactions.
